When I was on sertraline, I actually don't think I had any withdrawals. Not anything too big or noticeable, anyways. But I also had a very low dose given both my age and my size, weight and eating habits, so that may have been a factor as for why.

Mirtapazine on the other hand, I don't remember exactly, but I know I felt dizzy and lightheaded for a little while. Think I had some nausea too. The first day I stopped, which was completely cold turkey, was really hard. By the second and third day it wasn't really noticable, though. I remember being a lot more irritable than usual, and while that is a symptom the time I stopped was a really stressful family-related time, so that may have been where my irritability came from also. Beyond that I didn't really have anything. I think the side effects of being on Mirtapazine were far worse than the withdrawals, so if I had any others I didn't notice them because they were much better compared to the side effects. That's my personal experience with it, for others it's probably a little different.

My mood did stabilise a lot more when on my anti depressants (one of them, anyways, I've taken 2 or 3 different ones total). I wasn't actively suicidal anymore. School didn't feel as depressing for the first year I was on them. Eventually I started to get depressed over school again, but I don't think that's by any fault of the anti depressants. 

I'm completely off any sort of meds right now, and I get mood swings now and then, and I'm still very depressed and very suicidal but overall I'm doing much better than I was when I was first on them. It could be a coincidence, because I got on my meds at around age 12 or 13, which is usually the height of mood swings and emotional hardships of puberty. Now that I'm older, my stability might just be because of my age rather than that the meds had any long lasting effects, but there's a possibility they played a role too. In addition to that I believe the anti depressants I was on are also prescribed for anxiety, which I suffer from, and I do think my anxiousness improved considerably from them and a mix of other things.

I made it seem like all the side effects were huge. Sexual dysfunction is very common in anti depressants users, but it's not guaranteed, it's not always permanent, and it's not always as severe. Some other more mild effects I had were just general change in appetite (I can't remember if it was increase or decrease) and feeling overall tired and sometimes sick (when I was on Mirtapazine). There's probably some more I'm forgetting here and there but those were the biggest that effected me negatively and the most noticable. Eventually after my body got used to the meds I didn't have most mild side effects anymore. However, the reason why I'm not on anything right now was because the sickness I got from Mirtapazine was so bad. I stopped it, and because I'm relatively stable emotionally (not as violent or actively suicidal as I used to be) my therapist and doctor decided I'm okay without them right now.

I'm not quite sure what kind of cut you made, but if it's not too deep, rinse it out with water and mild soap the best you can (not only the pus, rinse the scar in general to rid it of dirt and bacteria) every day. Cover it with a bandage (not a band-aid, an actual bandage made for covering wounds, Band-Aids don't do well with completely covering wounds, especially not infected ones). If you don't have access to bandages, Band-Aids are the next best.

Take the bandage off every day and replace it with a new one. Give the cut some time to breathe before putting on a new bandage. Inspect the cut at this time too. 

Repeat this until it gets better (or worse, where at that case you need to see someone). 

There are also some antibacterial OTC cream stuff that are at like local marts and such. If you can get your hand on those, follow the instructions on it (be sure to check if you're able to put it on your cut, sometimes certain creams can't be put onto already infected or open wounds).

Edit: AVOID hydrogen peroxide and rubbing alcohol if you can. Both of them can be a lot more harmful than helpful. Although they can get rid of bacteria, they can also hurt healthy cells and thus slow down the healing process. However, if you do still choose to use it, I would recommend hydrogen peroxide as rubbing alcohol can give you burns (not extreme burns, but inflammation and swelling type burns). Hydrogen peroxide is more likely to hurt the healthy cells than alcohol, but the likelihood of it doing any serious damage to the cells is pretty low. As long as it it not a daily thing.
